s01.text: Twenty-six gigabytes of AI, squeezed into nine hundred megabytes. And it still works.

s02.text: This is Samsung's LittleBit. A thirteen-billion-parameter model, at zero point one bits per weight.

s03.text: Which should be impossible. One bit is a single yes or no. A tenth of a bit is nothing at all.

s04.text: So they stopped storing weights. No rounding down. No smaller numbers. They deleted the numbers.

s05.text: A weight matrix becomes two thin matrices, holding nothing but plus one and minus one.

s06.text: Multiply them, and the original comes back. The big matrix is never saved. It's rebuilt on the fly.

s07.text: That's how the cost falls below one bit. The information is shared, not stored.

s08.text: Samsung calls it latent factorization. Then they add compensation, to recover what the signs throw away.

s09.text: Thirty-one times less memory. Eleven times faster than full precision, by their estimate.

s10.text: And the quality matches one-bit models, at one tenth of their bits.

s11.text: This is how AI ends up on your phone, your laptop, your watch.
